key_insight: Block-triangular joint drifting turns ordinary one-step trajectory data into a one-step generative surrogate by preserving the current-state marginal while directly sampling the conditional next-state distribution.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast stochastic simulation with only one model evaluation per time step, making it attractive for uncertainty quantification and large-scale scientific computing workflows.
method: Apply drift not to next-state conditionals alone, but to the empirical joint distribution of consecutive states.
Use a block-triangular architecture so the first component preserves the current-state marginal and the second component generates the next state conditionally.
Produce stochastic trajectories without auxiliary intermediate generative steps between time steps.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments showing accurate marginal and trajectory-dependent statistics, with favorable accuracy-cost tradeoffs versus deterministic, diffusion-, flow-, and distillation-based surrogates.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well the projected joint drift is learned from limited one-realization-per-state trajectory data and on preserving stability across long rollouts.
paper_title: One-Step Generative Surrogate Models via Block-Triangular Joint Drifting
